newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 28.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - December 28.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy
The Hindustan Times
NO PLAN TO TOPPLE GOVERNMENT: CONGRESS CHIEF

Communist Party of India (Marxist) general secretary H.S. Surjeet called on Congress president Sitarm Kesri, seeking to know whether the Congress planned to withdraw support to the United Front (UF) government in the near future. Congress sources said Kesri assured Surjeet that the Congress had no such plan after the election of new Congress Parliamentary Party leader on January 3. Kesri, however, said the Congress would review the performance of the United Front government periodically.
The Times of India
FEAR OF INVESTIGATION BENUMBS OFFICIALS, MINISTERS

With the increasing political uncertainty at the Centre, the UF government has been gripped by inertia. Important decisions are either not being taken or are delayed. It is so because both secretaries and ministers fear the consequences if such decisions are followed by departmental inquiries or a probe by the Central Bureau of Investigation. The situation has been compounded by the failure of the UF government to gain political legitimacy, demonstrated by the setback it suffered in its quest to form a government in Uttar Pradesh.
Indian Express
GOVERNMENT NOT TO FIX OIL PRICES

Pricing of petroleum and petro products should be taken out of the government's purview, the petroleum ministry suggested. The ministry instead recommended fixing of prices by the oil coordination commitee (OCC) comprising officials of various state-owned oil companies. But, prior to shifting the pricing onus to the OCC, the ministry sought a hike in prices of petroleum products to partially offset the 155 billion rupee deficit in the oil pool account. An earlier recommendation for a 15 percent hike in oil prices was opposed by the ruling coalition, fearing a political backlash.
The Economic Times
BROKERS WANT GENERAL ACCOUNTING PRACTICE FOR COMPANIES

Upset with fudging of balance sheets by companies, market representatives asked for the introduction of a general accounting practice (GAP). At a meeting of the parliamentary standing committee on finance, market representatives said incorrect balance sheets had misled investors and was partly responsible for their lack of confidence in the stock markets. Besides GAP, the market intermediaries recommended the removal of minimum alternate tax, revival of forward trading and abolition of double taxation in order to revive the markets.
PUBLIC DISTRIBUTION SOP TO BENEFIT 350 MLN

In consonance with the United Front's minimum programme, the government has decided to fashion a revamped public distribution system (PDS). The new system, to supply foodgrain at half the prevailing PDS price, is expected to benefit 350 million people living below the poverty line. It is also in sharp contrast to the existing system of providing universal access to foodgrain through the PDS.
STATES GET MORE POWERS IN MINING

The powers for renewal of prospecting licences and mining leases have been delegated to the state government. Minister of Steel and Mines B.P. Baishya also announced the setting up of a committee to look into the steps required to stop illegal mining, streamline procedures pertaining to grant of prospecting licenses and mining leases. The panel would suggest measures to reduce delays both at central and state levels. The minister said his ministry also proposed to set a time frame within which this committee would submit its report.
MEGA MERGER OF FINANCIAL INSTITUTIONS PLANNED

The boards of Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) and SCICI Ltd has decided to meet on December 31, to consider a merger of the two companies. The move aims at creating a financial giant with assets in excess of 330 billion rupees. Industry and the financial community celebrated the announcement by speculating on the possible swap ratio, which would be officially announced on December 31. Market sources anticipated the swap ratio to be around two shares of ICICI for every five shares of SCICI held. While ICICI's equity base currently stands at 3.97 billion rupees, SCICI's is at 2.46 billion rupees.
MINISTRY MAY TRIP GRID PRIVATISATION

The Power Ministry will recommend the privatisation of power transmission systems to be confined to construction of new power lines and their maintenance. The private sector will, therefore, not be allowed to operate transmission lines and charge revenue for it, thus making the privatisation process only partial. Government sources said this was designed to encourage private sector participation in the sector, but operation of lines would remain the preserve of the state power utilities (SEBs) and the Power Grid Corporation (PGCIL). The government planned to allow private parties to set up the lines on their own or through joint ventures with the SEBs and PGCIL.
Financial Express
FINANCIAL INSTITUTION LOANS DIP 39 PCT IN NOVEMBER

Disbursements by financial institutions (FIs) fell sharply by about 39 percent to 16.28 billion rupees in November this year. The figure stood at 26.64 billion rupees in the corresponding period last year. However, the total disbursements in the eight-month period ended November were still higher by 14 percent at 239.87 billion rupees against 210.47 billion rupees in November last year. FI sources did not rule out a further fall in the growth rate of disbursements in the next couple of months.
FOREIGN INVESTORS HOLD THE KEY TO SWAP RATIO

Overseas investors hold the key to the ICICI-SCICI merger swap ratio. Foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and foreign holding by way of GDRs together account for about 25 percent of ICICI's equity. Sources feel the boards of ICICI and SCICI are likely to fix the swap ratio at 1:2.5. The exchange ratio could be fixed at anywhere between two and three SCICI shares for each ICICI share, sources said. Considering the existing parameters, the proposed merger is likely to be more beneficial to the shareholders of SCICI.
Business Standard
TELECOM MAJOR TO LAUNCH GDR ISSUE IN FEBRUARY

The global depository receipts issue of Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) would hit international markets in February next year. Financial analysts working on it expect it to be priced around 1,150 rupees a share. VSNL would undertake a series of pre-issue, soft roadshows in mid-January. Sources said the soft roadshows would serve the dual purpose of getting an indicative price at which investors would pick up the issue and also give a feedback on the investors' commitments.
INDIAN AIRLINES POSTS 58 MLN RUPEE OPERATING PROFIT

Indian Airlines (IA) earned an operating profit of 58 million rupees against the projected loss of 151.8 million rupees in the first half of fiscal 1996/97 (April-March). Sources said the indications were that the ailing national carrier would come out of the red in the next financial year. IA sources attributed the turnaround to two factors - a sharp drop in the market share of private airlines and increased aircraft utilisation.
ORDINANCE ON FINANCIAL BODIES, PORTS PLANNED

The cabinet decided to promulgate an ordinance to amend the Reserve Bank of India Act to regulate non-banking and unincorporated financial bodies. The finance minister had earlier announced the government's intention to regulate blade companies that are not governed by central bank guidelines. The cabinet also decided to promulgate an ordinance on the Indian Port Trust Act and the Major Port Trust Act. The port-related ordinance would pave the way for appointment of an independent regulatory authority to fix and revise port tariffs.
DISCLOSURE OF UNUTILISED ISSUE PROCEEDS MANDATORY

The Department of Company Affairs brought about a crucial amendment in the Companies Act, making it mandatory for corporates to disclose unutilised issue proceeds in their balance sheets. Companies raising funds from the international markets through issue of global depository receipts would also have to provide details about the unutilised funds in their financial statements. Sources said a funds flow statement on the unused proceeds would bring in greater transparency in accounting practices.
Business Line
TEN STATE OWNED FIRMS EXCEED OUTPUT TARGETS

Ten manufacturing public sector undertakings (PSUs) under the Department of Heavy Industries (DHI) exceeded their respective targeted production for the month of November 1996. The PSUs exceeding their targets are led by Bharat Ophthalmic Glass (326 percent), Hindustan Salts (230 percent), Bharat Process and Mechanical Engineering Co (150 percent), Scooters India (131 per cent), National Industrial Development Corporation (120 percent), Richardson and Cruddas Ltd (117 percent), Bharat Wagon and Engineering Co (110 percent), Reyroll Burn (109 percent), Braithwaite and Co (109 percent) and Bharat Breaks and Valves (103 percent).
